The popcorn machine, grey machine, straw cup and monitor stand on the counter and are decor. The counter top is thin (3 rows) but has a distinct edge line and shadow. styleAnswer.evidence: On the measured facts the candidate is close to the stall-cheese and well references: 16 visible tones per tile against 17 and 20, and 0% near-flat coverage. Density alone would not fail it. The outline is the problem. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so it uses the uniform dark grey/black line around the machine, register and counter that marks the 'sticker' look. The Beodeul stall, hedge and well use tinted dark-material edges (1%, 0% and 33% neutral). Each material on the candidate (the red/white striped counter, the grey machines, the popcorn) shows only about 3 lightness steps, against 5-6 on the references. Texture is limited to a few stripe and screen details with no per-material grain, and the pieces are separated by outline rather than by value. A careful artist would not accept it next to the stall reference without it looking flatter and more outlined.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a popcorn machine, register and striped counter. Density is fine on the numbers: 16 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, with 0% near-flat coverage. The problem is structure. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, and by eye the dark line around the machine, register and counter is uniform and colourless. Beodeul instead uses dark brown, green or red-brown edges tinted to the neighbouring material (cheese stall 1% neutral, hedge 0%, well 33%). That is the sticker look. The red/white counter stripes and the grey register body are close to flat two- or three-step blocks, with little per-material ramping or grain. The popcorn has some speckle but few steps. Overall it is cleanly drawn but shallower than the stall and well references, with about 3 steps per material against their 5-6.
